faqs.question: Where can I get the latest version of the Epson Communication Driver for my printer?
faqs.answer: Download the Communication Driver from the Downloads tab on your product's support page.

faqs.question: Can I use the printer without the waste ink bottle installed?
faqs.answer: No, the waste ink bottle must be installed at all times to capture waste ink, which is a by-product of printing. Make sure the waste ink bottle is installed even when the printer is not powered on.

faqs.question: Can I use an expired ink cartridge in my printer?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend using expired ink cartridges in the printer. Do not use an unopened ink cartridge if the date on the package has expired. For best results, use ink cartridges before the expiration date printed on the package (and within six months of installation in the printer). Replace expired cartridges with new ones.
You may need to replace a cartridge that is more than six months old, if your printouts do not look their best, even after cleaning and aligning the printhead. We recommend you store any unused or unopened ink cartridges in a cool, dark place.

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: No, Adobe Photoshop is not a postscript application and does not require a RIP.

faqs.question: My printer's ink cartridges are half full after I install the first set of ink cartridges. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer: Ink from the first set of ink cartridges is used to charge the printer's ink delivery system. This will not happen again when you install new ink cartridges.

faqs.question: Why does the printer have a waste ink bottle?
faqs.answer: The waste ink bottle is used to collect waste ink and must be emptied periodically. See the product's User's Guide for waste ink disposal guidelines.

faqs.question: I see the message Ink Cartridge Error: Replace Ink Cartridge. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
An ink cartridge in your printer needs to be replaced. The cartridge may be expended, or the IC chip on the cartridge may not be communicating properly. Try reseating the cartridge and turning the printer off and on. If you still see the error message, try installing a different ink cartridge in the printer.
If this did not solve the problem, contact Epson support.

faqs.question: When should I clean the suction cap?
faqs.answer:
You need to clean the suction cap whenever you see a message on the LCD screen or at the end of every week that you use the printer. You may also need to clean the suction cap if you experience difficulty cleaning nozzles after performing a nozzle check. Even if the message is not displayed, follow the steps here to clean the suction cap.
Note:
If you continue to use the printer without cleaning the suction cap, the ink nozzles may clog and print quality may decline.
Turn on the printer.
Press the
maintenance button. The Maintenance menu appears.
Press the up or down arrow button to select
Head Cap Cleaning
, and press the right arrow button to select it.
Press the up or down arrow button to select
Yes
, and press the
OK
button. The platen and print head move to the maintenance position.
Caution:
Do not move the print head or the platen manually. A malfunction may occur.
Note:
A buzzer sounds after 10 minutes once the platen and print head move to the maintenance position. Press the
OK
button to continue cleaning. The buzzer sounds again after 10 minutes. Nozzles can be clogged if more time passes, so finish cleaning as soon as possible.
Open the printer cover.
If a film of waste ink has built up on the suction cap, remove it with the supplied plastic tweezers.
Caution:
Use only the supplied plastic tweezers. Be careful not to damage the suction cap. If the suction cap is damaged, air may leak and the print head may become dry or difficult to clean.
Wipe the inside of the suction cap using a thin cleaning swab dampened with ink cleaning solution. Rotate the swab as you wipe.
Caution:
Make sure ink cleaner does not drip onto the anti-drying caps to the right of the suction cap. If any cleaner does drip, wipe it with a dry cleaning swab. If cleaner is left on the anti-drying caps, the print head nozzles could become clogged.
Wipe the outside of the suction cap with a large cleaning swab dampened with ink cleaning solution.
Wipe the top edge of the suction cap with a large cleaning swab dampened with ink cleaning solution.
If necessary, remove any excess ink from the edges of the cap.
Close the printer cover.
Press the
OK
button. The print head returns to its normal position and the Settings menu closes.
Perform a nozzle check.

faqs.question: What is the capacity of the waste ink bottle?
faqs.answer: Its capacity is 2 liters; however, the product will prompt you to replace the bottle when it is at 1.5 liters capacity.

faqs.question: How often should I shake the ink cartridges?
faqs.answer:
To maintain print quality, you must do the following:
Shake the White ink cartridges at the start of every working day or when a message is displayed.
Shake the color ink cartridges at least once a month.
Shake each cartridge as shown below. For new ink cartridges, rapidly shake each cartridge for about 15 seconds. For White ink, flip the cartridge over as shown and repeat.
Caution:
Do not touch the IC chip on the end of each cartridge; otherwise, the cartridge may not be recognized, or the printer may not print properly.
Related tasks
Shaking and Replacing the Ink Cartridges

faqs.question: Can I print on polyester T-shirts?
faqs.answer:
Yes, you can print on T-shirts with a minimum 50/50 cotton/polyester blend, but your print quality may vary. Printing on materials with high polyester content will result in more subdued colors. It is recommended to perform a test print first.
For best results, use a T-shirt that is 100% cotton with thick and tightly-woven (ringspun) material.

faqs.question: The print quality is uneven, too light, or too dark, or lines appear in the printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If you notice that your print quality is uneven, too light, too dark, or there are lines in the print (banding), try these solutions:
Run a nozzle check to see if any of the print head nozzles are clogged. Then clean the print head, if necessary.
If the print surface is too far from the print head, the following problems may occur:
Lines in the image (banding)
Edges of the image are blurry
Text and straight lines are duplicated
Image is grainy
Adjust the platen height.
Print in uni-directional mode to see if the platen height adjustment is off.
Align the print head.
Perform a feed adjustment.
Make sure you are using genuine Epson ink cartridges. If you use non-Epson ink cartridges, the printed result may be faint or the colors may be inaccurate because the remaining ink level is not correctly detected.
Make sure your ink cartridges have not expired. For best results, use ink cartridges before the expiration date printed on the package (within a year of installation in the printer). Replace expired cartridges with new ones.
Shake the cartridges thoroughly before installing them in the printer. To maintain optimum print quality, remove and shake the installed White ink cartridge at the start of every working day or when a message is displayed. Shake the color cartridges once a month.
Compare the printed result with the image on your computer screen. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
Make sure that the printer cover is closed during printing.
Check the ink levels on the LCD screen. Replace any cartridges that are low on ink.
Adjust the print quality settings in the Garment Creator software to a higher quality setting.
Adjust the density of the White ink in the Garment Creator software.
Make sure the pre-treatment solution is not too diluted. If the pre-treatment solution has been diluted too much, the solidity of the White ink is weakened and the edges of the image may be blurred. Try reducing the density of the White ink in the Garment Creator software or use a stronger pre-treatment solution.

faqs.question: Does Epson offer RIP software for the product?
faqs.answer:
No, Epson does not offer RIP software for the printer. RIP software is available from third-party vendors. Check with an Epson authorized reseller for available options.

The product comes with the Garment Creator software for printing.

faqs.question: Does an alarm sound when an error occurs?
faqs.answer:
Yes, the buzzer sounds if the Alert Sound Setting is on. The setting is turned on by default.
If you need to turn on this setting, press the right arrow button on the control panel to display the menu screen. Use the arrow buttons to select the
Administrator
menu and then select
Preferences
>
Alert Sound Setting
>
On
.

faqs.question: How do I print a nozzle check pattern?
faqs.answer:
See below.
Performing a Nozzle Check
To maintain optimum print quality, perform a nozzle check before printing.
If the platen is not in the forward position, press the
moveable base button to move it forward.
Make sure that spacers a and b are installed.
Make sure that the medium-size (standard) platen or grip pad is installed.
Remove the platen frame.
Place one sheet of A4- or letter-size plain paper on the center of the platen or grip pad. Secure the corners with tape.
Set the height adjustment lever to the
P
position if you are using a platen or the
1
position if you are using a grip pad.
Press the
maintenance button on the control panel. The Maintenance menu appears.
Press the right arrow button to select
Nozzle Check
.
Press the
OK
button twice. The nozzle check pattern prints onto the paper.
Remove the paper and check the printed pattern:
If there are no gaps in the pattern, the nozzles are clean.
If there are gaps in the pattern, clean the print head.
Note:
A complete nozzle cleaning is required only if there are more than 3 nozzles missing and the gaps are adjacent to each other. Otherwise, cleaning is not required.
Replace the platen frame.
Related tasks
Adjusting the Height of the Platen
Attaching or Removing Spacers
Cleaning the Print Head

faqs.question: Can I purchase a heat press from Epson?
faqs.answer:
No, Epson does not provide heat presses. Contact an Epson authorized reseller for more information about recommended heat press equipment.
Note:
Your heat press needs to be larger than your platen and able to sustain a temperature of 338 °F (170 °C) or more for 90 seconds. Check the accuracy of your heat press temperature with a probe; temperatures exceeding 356 °F may result in dull colors. For best results, use a heat press with a piece of parchment (silicone) paper or a Teflon (fluoro-resin) sheet at low pressure to allow the steam to escape.

faqs.question: Does Epson sell automatic pre-treatment equipment?
faqs.answer: No, Epson does not sell automatic pre-treatment equipment for direct-to-garment printing. Contact an Epson authorized reseller for information about recommended equipment.
